title: The widow didn’t come to Elisha with a business plan.
paragraphs: The widow didn’t come to Elisha with a business plan.
She came with an empty house.

Debt behind her.
Fear in front of her.
Her sons almost taken from her.
And then the prophet asked the question that exposed everything:
“What hast thou in the house?” — 2 Kings 4:2

Not, “What did you lose?”
Not, “Who abandoned you?”
Not, “How bad is it?”
But…
What is still left?
She said, “Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.”
Only oil.
That was her sentence.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
What she called only, God called enough to begin a miracle.

God saw it.
The tears.
The panic.
The private conversations where you wondered how you would survive.
The moments you looked at your life and said, “I have nothing left.”
But God does not need what you lost to bless you.
He can start with what remains.

The widow had oil.
Moses had a rod.
David had a sling.
A boy had five loaves and two fish.
And you?

You may still have breath.
You may still have a prayer.
You may still have one broken “Lord, help me.”
That is not nothing.
Read that again.

The miracle did not begin when the jars were full.
It began when she obeyed while the jars were still empty.
“Go, borrow thee vessels abroad… borrow not a few.” — 2 Kings 4:3
Faith made room before provision arrived.
And this is where the Gospel meets you.
Sin empties us. Pride deceives us. Fear enslaves us. But Jesus Christ came for empty people.
“For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.” — Luke 19:10

You cannot save yourself.
You cannot pay the debt of sin.
You cannot manufacture grace.
But Jesus paid what you could never pay.

At the cross, He took the debt.
By His blood, He offers forgiveness.
Through repentance and faith, He gives new life.
“For by grace are ye saved through faith… not of works.” — Ephesians 2:8-9
So bring Him what is left.

Your shame.
Your exhaustion.
Your small faith.
Your oil.
Because in the hands of God, surrender becomes supply.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
